function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑use set of files** that you can drop into the `nodejs-welcome` repository.  
They cover:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Dockerfile` | Builds a lightweight Node.js image |
| `k8s/deployment-service.yaml` | Deployment + Service for Kubernetes |
| `.github/workflows/docker-image.yml` | GitHub Actions workflow that builds & pushes the image on every push to `main` |

> **NOTE** – The repo is a Node.js project, so the Dockerfile uses the official Node image.  
> The Kubernetes YAML assumes the image will be built locally and pushed to a registry (Docker Hub or GHCR).  
> The GitHub Actions workflow expects you to store your registry credentials as secrets (`DOCKERHUB_USERNAME`, `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` or `GHCR_TOKEN`).

---

## 1. Dockerfile

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile
# ------------------------------------
# Build a minimal Node.js image for the app
# ------------------------------------
FROM node:18-alpine

# Set working directory
WORKDIR /app

# Copy package files first to leverage Docker cache
COPY package*.json ./

# Install production dependencies only
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy the rest of the source code
COPY . .

# Expose the port the app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Start the application
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
```

> **Why this Dockerfile?**  
> * `node:18-alpine` is small and fast.  
> * `npm ci` guarantees a reproducible install.  
> * `EXPOSE 3000` matches the default port used by most Express apps.

---

## 2. Kubernetes YAML

Create a folder called `k8s` (or any name you prefer) and add `deployment-service.yaml` inside it.

```yaml
# k8s/deployment-service.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: yourdockerhubusername/nodejs-welcome:latest   # <-- change this
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 3000
```

> **What to change?**  
> * Replace `yourdockerhubusername` with your Docker Hub (or GHCR) username.  
> * If you want a different number of replicas or a different service type (`NodePort`, `LoadBalancer`), edit the `replicas` and `type` fields.

---

## 3. GitHub Actions Workflow

Create the directory `.github/workflows/` (if it doesn’t exist) and add `docker-image.yml`.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/docker-image.yml
name: Build and Push Docker image

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # 1️⃣ Checkout the repo
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # 2️⃣ Set up Docker Buildx (multi‑platform support)
      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

      # 3️⃣ Log in to Docker Hub (or GHCR)
      - name: Log in to Docker Hub
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          username: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}
          password: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}

      # 4️⃣ Build & push the image
      - name: Build and push Docker image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
        with:
          context: .
          push: true
          tags: yourdockerhubusername/nodejs-welcome:latest   # <-- change this
```

> **Secrets you’ll need**  
> * `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` – your Docker Hub username  
> * `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` – a Docker Hub access token (or password)  
>   *If you prefer GHCR, replace the login step with `docker/login-action@v3` using `GHCR_TOKEN` and adjust the image tag accordingly.*

---

## 4. Add, Commit & Push

Open a terminal in the root of the cloned repo and run:

```bash
# 1️⃣ Add the new files
git add Dockerfile k8s/deployment-service.yaml .github/workflows/docker-image.yml

# 2️⃣ Commit
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests, and CI workflow"

# 3️⃣ Push to main
git push origin main
```

> **Tip** – If you’re working on a feature branch, replace `main` with your branch name and merge later.

---

## 5. Verify

1. **Docker image** – After the push, check your Docker Hub (or GHCR) account; the image `nodejs-welcome:latest` should appear.  
2. **Kubernetes** – Apply the manifest:

   ```bash
   kubectl apply -f k8s/deployment-service.yaml
   ```

   Then verify pods and service:

   ```bash
   kubectl get pods
   kubectl get svc
   ```

3. **GitHub Actions** – Go to the *Actions* tab of the repo; you should see a successful run for the workflow.

---

### Recap

| Step | What you did |
|------|--------------|
| 1 | Cloned the repo |
| 2 | Created Dockerfile, Kubernetes YAML, and GitHub Actions workflow |
| 3 | Added files to Git |
| 4 | Committed & pushed to `main` |

You’re now set up with containerization, Kubernetes deployment, and continuous integration! 🚀
